page: Microsoft Azure D64a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor operating at 3.35 GHz. It provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 256.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include a GPU, but it bundles 1718 GB of local SSD storage.

Benchmark results highlight significant multi-core throughput alongside modest single-thread metrics. In PassMark testing, the CPU score reached 63075.82 and the memory benchmark achieved a top-tier rating of 3066.82, placing it in the top 10 percent. Multi-threaded evaluations demonstrate high capacity, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 17263.0, strong performance in software compilation (38830.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 298.78 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core evaluations show relative performance limitations, evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 776.69 in the bottom 10 percent and a Geekbench single-core score of 1610.0.

Hardware vector instruction support includes AVX, but lacks AVX-512 extensions and AMX units. CPU-based LLM inference reflects this profile, yielding strong throughput on smaller models (2533.88 tokens/sec prompt processing on 135M models) while scaling down to average tiers for medium and large models. Database operations and local caching operations perform reliably, highlighted by a PassMark database score of 26742.75 and Redis SET performance reaching 60.77 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the D64a_v4 lies in its parallel execution advantage versus per-core latency. Workloads requiring high per-thread burst speeds will experience bottlenecking, whereas horizontally scalable tasks benefit from the 64-thread allocation. The server functions efficiently for large compilation pipelines, multi-threaded data processing, relational database hosting, container clustering, and general enterprise backend workloads that leverage the 256 GB RAM pool and local SSD volume.
description: Microsoft Azure D64a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with an AMD EPYC 7452 processor featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores) running at 3.35 GHz, 256.0 GB of RAM, and 1718 GB of local SSD storage without GPU acceleration. It maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3066.82. Benchmark results reveal strong multi-core throughput, including a PassMark CPU score of 63075.82, 38830.0 in Clang compilation, and 26742.75 in database operations, balanced against modest single-core performance. The architecture supports AVX and standard cryptographic instructions, delivering solid efficiency for parallelized enterprise operations. The D64a_v4 is well configured for relational databases, extensive software builds, multi-threaded batch data transformations, and container host environments requiring dedicated core counts and local SSD cache.
